course_name_original: Management and economic of engineer projects
course_name_en: Management and economics of engineering projects

learning_outcomes.text: The student recognizes the constants and project variables and can define their mutual relations and impact on the project. Possesses basic knowledge necessary to understand the ex-technical and non-technical conditions of engineering activity, possesses basic knowledge on management, including quality management and running commercial enterprise, within the range of protection of intellectual property and patent law; knows general principles of creating and developing forms of individual entrepreneurship and basic HSE rules applicable to machine industry.

The student uses knowledge obtained under different modules to assess non-technical effects of engineering activities and adopts responsible attitudes. Understands ex-technical aspects of the activities included in the profession of a mechanical engineer, among others its social impact and influence on the condition of an environment; is aware of the responsibility connected with the decisions made in connection with engineering activity.

The student defines the rules for managing people in quality systems. The student knows and can apply the principles of leadership and motivating. The student understands the need to update owned knowledge and can identify and use sources of knowledge. The student knows the rules of Continuous Improvement and benefits from skillful use of human resource potential in terms of creativity and innovation. Is aware of the need for complementing the knowledge throughout the whole life, is able to select proper methods of teaching and learning, critically assesses the possessed knowledge; is aware of the importance of professional conduct and following the rules of professional ethics; is able to show resourcefulness and innovation in the realisation of professional projects.

syllabus_topics: Economic Engineering: Cost of Money, Transaction Elements, Nominal and Effective Interest Rates, etc.
Project Funds: Describing a Project, Value Analysis, Return Analysis, Accepting or Rejecting Decision Rules, Effects of Inflation.
Sensitivity and Risk Analysis: Risks, Risk Analysis, Expected Value and Variance of a Project, Decision Rule.
Investment Costs vs. Operating Costs, Minimum Cost Function.
Project Management: Projects and Programs, Management, Planning and Scheduling, Project Life Cycle, Project Phases, Milestones.
Team Building: Personality Types, Team Roles, Team Effectiveness.
Project Management: WBS, Gantt, Earned Value Method, Critical Path, Risk Management.

assessment_methods.method: Written credit in the lecture part
Final works of the practice part

assessment_rules: A passing threshold of 60.0% is required for both the written credit in the lecture part and the final works of the practice part. The final grade is composed of 50.0% from the written credit and 50.0% from the final works.
